title: Nine Wickets Down, One Ball Left. Chaudhary Chose to Swing.
excerpt: Mitchell Owen’s ferocious 77 off 35 balls and Nikhil Chaudhary’s last-ball six seal a one-wicket MLC thriller over Texas Super Kings at George Mason Stadium in Fairfax
body:
There are endings in cricket that arrive so suddenly they leave the crowd standing before the ball has cleared the rope. This was one of them.

With nine wickets down, five runs still needed, and Akeal Hosein running in for the final delivery of the match, Washington Freedom’s Nikhil Chaudhary swung through the line and sent the ball sailing over the boundary. Six runs. Game over. Freedom 187 for 9, Texas Super Kings 185 for 4. A one-wicket win that may define the 2026 Major League Cricket season.

Owen Sets the Table on Fire

The chase of 186 needed an accelerant, and Mitchell Owen supplied it with raw, unfiltered violence. The Australian all-rounder walked out and began hitting the ball as though he had a personal grievance against it. Seven fours, six sixes, 77 runs from just 35 deliveries at a strike rate of 220 — the kind of innings that makes everyone in the ground stop what they are doing and watch.

Owen’s assault gave Freedom a platform that looked impregnable. But T20 cricket is rarely that generous.

Captain Steve Smith anchored the middle overs with a measured 30 off 21 balls, lacing three sixes of his own. Between them, Owen and Smith put on the bulk of the chase. But once Owen departed, the wheels began to loosen.

Hosein’s Spell Almost Stole It

If Owen was the story of the first half of the chase, Akeal Hosein was the story of the second. The Trinidad left-arm spinner returned figures of 4 for 36 from his four overs, ripping through Freedom’s middle and lower order with a mix of guile and pace off the pitch. Adam Milne chipped in with 2 for 31, and suddenly the chase that had looked comfortable was anything but.

Freedom slipped from a position of control to nine wickets down, with five runs still required off the last ball of the match. Hosein had just had Asif Mehmood stumped two balls earlier. One more wicket and Texas would have stolen it.

How Texas Got to 185

The Super Kings had set the target on the back of a savage late acceleration from Wiaan Mulder and Donovan Ferreira. The pair came together at 110 for 4 in the 15th over and plundered 75 runs from just 31 balls in an unbeaten fifth-wicket stand that redefined the match.

Mulder finished with 43 not out off 20 balls, smashing four sixes, while Ferreira was even more destructive — 44 not out off 20 with five sixes and a four. Their assault turned what had been a middling effort into a commanding 185 for 4.

Earlier, Saiteja Mukkamalla (37 off 28) and Rilee Rossouw (34 off 24) had given the innings structure after Faf du Plessis fell cheaply for 8, caught behind off Lockie Ferguson. Chaudhary himself was impressive with the ball, returning 2 for 29 from his four overs to provide crucial breakthroughs through the middle overs, removing both Mukkamalla and Rossouw.

The Last Over

Hosein had the ball for the 20th over. He had already taken three wickets in his previous overs. On ball four, he struck again — Mehmood stumped, the ninth wicket down. The Freedom dressing room would have been reaching for their pads and helmets, preparing for the worst.

Lockie Ferguson, the last man in, took guard and somehow scrambled a leg bye off ball five. That brought Chaudhary back on strike for the final delivery with five runs still needed.

What happened next will echo around George Mason Stadium for years. Chaudhary picked up the length early, transferred his weight, and launched the ball over the boundary for six. Freedom’s dugout erupted. A match that Hosein’s brilliance had very nearly stolen was snatched back in the blink of an eye.

Cricket Comes to the Beltway — and Stays

George Mason Stadium in Fairfax, Virginia, sits in one of the densest Indian diaspora corridors in the United States. The Northern Virginia-DC-Maryland triangle is home to hundreds of thousands of Indian Americans, and MLC has planted a franchise right in their backyard. Matches like this — featuring Indian-origin players in pivotal roles, played at a venue reachable by metro and minivan — are exactly how the league cements itself into the community.

Chaudhary, who grew up playing cricket in American leagues, is the kind of player who makes MLC more than an imported product. He is the local story, the kid from the community who is sharing a dressing room with Steve Smith and Lockie Ferguson and hitting last-ball sixes when it counts.

What’s Next

Freedom face the San Francisco Unicorns later in the tournament, while the Super Kings take on the Seattle Orcas in a match they will want to win to firm up their playoff position. After this game, nobody in the MLC will want to write off the Freedom — or underestimate the value of having Nikhil Chaudhary at the other end when everything is on the line.

*Brief Scores: Texas Super Kings 185/4 in 20 overs (Donovan Ferreira 44*, Wiaan Mulder 43*, Saiteja Mukkamalla 37; Nikhil Chaudhary 2/29, Lockie Ferguson 1/31) lost to Washington Freedom 187/9 in 19.6 overs (Mitchell Owen 77, Steve Smith 30; Akeal Hosein 4/36, Adam Milne 2/31) by 1 wicket.*
